rollback_procedure.trigger: Any acceptance test fails in production, form submissions drop, the WhatConverts swap stops, or conversions stop recording.
steps: 1. Revert the GTM container to the previously published version. This is immediate and reverses all tag changes on its own.
2. Restore the Divi child theme from the pre-change snapshot.
3. Restore the Gravity Forms form 1 configuration from the pre-change export.
4. Restore the five Divi page layouts from the Divi Library revision history.
5. If entry data is affected, restore the WordPress database from the pre-change backup. Only do this if entries were lost, because it also rolls back any genuine leads captured since the backup.
6. Re-run AT-4, AT-10, AT-11 and AT-12 to confirm the site is back to its prior state.
rollback_procedure.recovery_time_objective: GTM revert under 5 minutes; theme and form restore under 30 minutes; full database restore under 2 hours.
rollback_procedure.data_loss: None expected. The only destructive step is the database restore, which is last resort and would lose leads captured after the backup point.

corrected_deduplication_language.lead_id_does: Prevents repeat firing within the SAME Google Ads conversion action (6885463625), via transaction_id.
corrected_deduplication_language.lead_id_does_not: Does NOT deduplicate two different conversion actions. It will not stop WC Lead 7643656486 from also counting a submission that 6885463625 counted.
corrected_deduplication_language.never_describe_as: Cross-action deduplication. That does not exist in Google Ads.
corrected_deduplication_language.the_actual_control: Exactly one conversion action Primary and counted per physical lead event. That is a Google Ads configuration decision, pending the WhatConverts console answers, not a landing-page change.

google_ads_impact.note: ZERO Google Ads API mutations. The Google Ads conversion tag is reconfigured inside GTM, which is a GTM change.
